quick.summary: Why a precise number can lose a room, and three ways to make findings easy to hear.
quick.takeaway: Round it. One point per chart. Plain words.

beats.line: I showed conversion to four decimal places. Why did everyone glaze over?
The extra digits looked important, so they tried to read them.
Three habits. First, round to what changes the decision.
Second, one point per chart, so nobody hunts for it.
Third, plain words. Say the share of visitors who paid, not conversion rate.
The exact number stays in your notes. The room needs the useful one.
About three and a half percent of visitors paid, up half a point since spring.
Everyone heard that the first time.

quiz.question: How should you show conversion of 3.4721 percent to a product team?
options: Somewhere between one and ten percent
quiz.explanation: Rounding to the level that matters for the decision makes it easy to hear and remember.

quiz.question: Showing more decimal places always makes a finding more trustworthy.
quiz.explanation: Extra digits suggest precision the decision does not need and make the point harder to follow.
